common_mistakes: Starting the panel swap before the permit is issued and posted — Gilbert can stop the job and require corrections before inspection
Failing to include a load calculation for the 200 amp service upgrade — this is a common plan review rejection point
Missing grounding electrode or bonding corrections during the upgrade — inspectors will fail the job if the grounding system is incomplete
Not coordinating the utility meter pull/reconnect before scheduling the changeover — the crew can get stuck with the service dead
Submitting the application under the wrong permit type instead of an electrical service upgrade/panel replacement

pro_tips: Have the ROC license number, panel cut sheet, and load calc ready before opening the portal — that is what keeps a service upgrade moving same-day in many Arizona cities.
Call the utility first to line up the meter pull; the city permit may be quick, but utility scheduling is often the real bottleneck.
If the existing panel is crowded or the service mast needs replacement, include that in the original scope so you do not get hit with a second permit or revision later.
Coordinate utility meter release, grounding/bonding, panel schedule, service-load calculation, and inspection timing before any service shutdown.
